svg.aria-label: KPipe vs Atleon vs Confluent Parallel Consumer vs Reactor Kafka vs Kafka Share Consumer vs raw KafkaConsumer plus virtual threads: parallel-consumer throughput by ordering guarantee, allocation, and GC
svg.text: JMH throughput + gc profiler · 25,000 records · 8 partitions · 1,000 keys · forks=5 · iter=5 · Testcontainers Kafka 4.3.0 · Apple M3 Max · JDK 25.0.2 · capture 2026-10-12 (Atleon rerun 2026-10-13)
records / second · higher is better · whiskers are JMH 99.9% error
Per-key ordered arms (compare these with each other, not with the unordered panel)
records / second · higher is better · whiskers are JMH 99.9% error
bytes allocated per record · lower is better
GC events in the measurement window
GC time in the measurement window
• Unordered, no work: KPipe 574k, raw 547k and Atleon 614k are within about 12% of each other.
• Unordered, blocking work: Atleon 867k to 938k, raw 576k to 541k, KPipe 236k to 230k with error bands of about ±25%.
• Per key: Atleon leads KPipe by 4.0x to 5.4x, and KPipe leads Confluent KEY by 1.4x to 3.7x.
• gc.count and gc.time are totals for the measurement window, so faster arms run more invocations and collect more.
Per-partition arms and the single-threaded baseline are omitted: different guarantee. Full table: benchmarks/results/2026-10-12-full-suite.md
